newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rebound on snap election news.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rebound on snap election news.

text.p: French stocks opened higher on Tuesday after President Jacques Chirac dissolved parliament and set snap elections for May-June, seeking a mandate to bring France into monetary union.

"The market is up because one element of uncertainty has been lifted, but it doesn't mean a lot. There is very little volume, bidding is thin on all issues. It's a wait-and-see attitude," said one trader.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 5.34 points or 0.21 percent, at 2,528.01, at 0900 GMT, partially rebounding from a 0.98 percent decline on Monday.
Volume was a thin 536 million francs at 0830 GMT.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up five points at 2,527.
Traders said shares rose after two days of declining prices on Chirac's confirmation of early elections, which had been set for March and now will take place on May 25 and June 1.
They also predicted the market would be volatile and driven by opinion polls during the pre-election period.
Underlining the uncertainty ahead, the government delayed for a month the partial privatisation of France Telecom, which had been scheduled to begin in early May.
Clarins shares fell two percent on its 1996 results.
The skincare company reported a 1996 net attributable profit of 241.2 million francs, up 17.5 percent from 205.2 million francs.
A Sofres poll conducted before Chirac called the snap election showed investors were already growing more cautious about the outlook for the Bourse.
The poll published in the financial daily La Tribune found that 31 percent expected the Bourse to rise compared to 58 percent in January.
The CAC-40 has risen by 32 percent since January 1.
